TO: Commercial Sales Organization, Reconstructive Division
FROM: Carlos Mendes, Senior Product Manager, ApexHip
CC: Marcus Lee, VP Sales; Jenna Whitfield, Regional Sales Manager; Priya Raman, Director Quality & Complaint Handling; Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs
DATE: February 2, 2024
SUBJECT: Sales Guidance & Talking Points: ApexHip Voluntary Market Withdrawal

1. Administrative Overview & Logistics

Effective immediately, Friday, February 2, 2024, Veridian Orthopedics is initiating a voluntary commercial market withdrawal of the ApexHip Total Hip System (including all modular femoral heads, stems, and KinetiCoat acetabular cups).

All territory managers, sales representatives, and independent distributors must immediately pause any planned surgical implantations scheduled for Monday, February 5, onward. Coordination for return authorization numbers (RGA) and retrieval of hospital consignment and trunk inventory will commence next week via a structured inventory recovery portal managed through Agile PLM. Please ensure your accounts do not transfer stock between facilities.

While our primary immediate operational focus is inventory reconciliation and customer support, we recognize that surgeons, OR coordinators, and hospital risk managers will reach out to you with clinical and logistical inquiries throughout the day.

2. Clinical and Regulatory Context

To understand the environment prompting incoming surgeon contacts, reps should understand the context that has developed over recent reporting cycles. As communicated previously, international registry data—specifically the UK National Joint Registry (NJR) annual reporting which noted a cumulative 5-year revision rate of 7.1% for ApexHip (against an overall metal-on-metal benchmark of 3.2%)—alongside subsequent AJRR registry signals, led to our September 2021 Registry Signal Review and the October 2021 labeling update regarding patient positioning and cup inclination.

The decision announced today reflects leadership's ongoing evaluation of long-term commercial positioning in light of global MoM clinical registry trends and evolving reconstructive practice standards.

3. Approved Field Guidance: What to Say

When communicating with orthopaedic surgeons, surgical teams, and account administrators, stick strictly to the following approved messaging pillars:

*   Voluntary Action: "Veridian has elected to execute a proactive, voluntary market withdrawal of the ApexHip system from global distribution, effective February 2, 2024. This is a business and product line portfolio decision."
*   Asymptomatic Patients: "For patients currently implanted with ApexHip, the company is *not* recommending proactive surgical revision or prophylactic intervention in the absence of symptoms. Surgeons should continue standard postoperative follow-up protocols as outlined in the Instructions for Use (IFU)."
*   Symptomatic Inquiries & Medical Escalation: "If a patient presents with unresolved groin pain, swelling, or concerns regarding local tissue response, please advise the clinical team to evaluate per their standard clinical judgment. Do not offer medical advice or speculate on blood ion testing."
*   Dedicated Hotline Referral: Direct all technical, patient, or adverse-event inquiries directly to our dedicated Medical & Quality Information Hotline at extension 4880 (or via email at `clinicalsupport@veridianortho.com`), which is staffed and managed directly by Priya Raman’s Quality & Complaint Handling team. TrackWise intake numbers will be provided for any surgeon reporting an adverse event.

4. Critical Boundaries: What NOT to Say

To ensure alignment and prevent misinformation, field personnel are instructed to adhere strictly to the following restrictions:

*   Do NOT conflate this action with the 2022 coating recall. The June 2022 Class II recall (FDA Recall Z-1418-2022) involving Cork plasma-spray cup lots V-2200 through V-2299 was a distinct, isolated manufacturing adhesion issue that was fully remediated and closed. Do not discuss the coating recall in the same breath as this withdrawal; doing so creates profound clinical confusion regarding product wear vs. coating integrity.
*   Do NOT debate metal ion concentrations or registries. Never minimize NJR or AJRR data, but do not debate blood serum cobalt/chromium thresholds or adverse local tissue reaction (ALTR/ARMD) mechanisms with clinicians.
*   Do NOT comment on legal matters. If asked about ongoing product liability litigation or plaintiff filings, state clearly: "As a commercial representative, I cannot comment on legal or corporate proceedings. I can connect you directly with Veridian’s corporate communications department."

5. Next Steps

Inventory count sheets will be distributed by Operations by 5:00 PM EST today. Regional managers will hold alignment calls this afternoon. Please direct immediate process questions to Jenna Whitfield or Marcus Lee.

Dear Dr. Anand,

On behalf of Veridian Orthopedics, Inc., please find below our formal response to the Agency's May 8, 2019 inquiry regarding the ApexHip Total Hip System (510(k) K162447 / Post-Market Review). Attached to this submission is our detailed MDR and TrackWise complaint trending summary (Attachment 1: ApexHip_MDR_Trending_Analysis_2019.pdf).

Summary of Post-Market Surveillance Trending and Engineering Assessment:

1. Complaint Trending: A comprehensive review of our post-market surveillance database (TrackWise) confirms that exactly 14 metal-ion related complaints (associated with elevated cobalt/chromium levels, suspected ARMD, or early revision) have been logged since commercial launch in April 2017 through April 30, 2019. This represents an overall reporting rate of less than 0.2% across all commercially distributed ApexHip acetabular cups and femoral heads during this period, which remains well below internal statistical alert thresholds established under SOP-QC-408.

2. Clinical and Engineering Evaluation: In coordination with Medical Affairs and R&D Engineering, Veridian has reviewed available clinical histories and explant reports. A substantial proportion of reported events exhibit localized surgical variables, including high cup abduction angles. While the company's PMS program continues to closely monitor this trend, the cumulative data indicate that the device performs in accordance with its cleared safety profile. Consequently, no design change or corrective action has been deemed necessary at this time based on available clinical data.

Veridian remains fully committed to regulatory compliance under 21 CFR Part 803 and 21 CFR 820.198 and will continue providing routine updates as required.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo

Leon, I specifically need your eyes on Question 4 below. We want to be very careful with our positioning around historical marketing claims while still reassuring concerned patients:

Q4: Why was ApexHip recommended to me if it is now being withdrawn?
A: Total hip replacement decisions are made collaboratively between patients and their surgeons based on individual anatomy and clinical needs. ApexHip was marketed based on long-term performance data available at the time, specifically targeting active adult patients seeking joint stability and low volumetric wear. MEMORANDUM

To: Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs
From: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
Date: June 30, 2020
Subject: ApexHip Complaint Trending Report - H1 2020

This memorandum summarizes ApexHip complaint activity entered in TrackWise from January 1 through June 30, 2020. The review was conducted per the approved complaint trending procedure and includes complaints received from direct customer contacts, sales representatives, distributors, and surgeon offices. Duplicate reports concerning the same patient event were consolidated where identified.

A total of 68 ApexHip complaints were logged during H1 2020. Of these, 31 complaints relate to elevated cobalt and/or chromium ion values, suspected adverse reaction to metal debris (ARMD), unexplained pain with metal-on-metal bearing concerns, or imaging findings that may be consistent with local tissue reaction. This compares with 19 complaints in the corresponding H1 2019 period.

The increase is notable, although several of the 2020 reports concern implants placed in 2017 and 2018 and therefore reflect a growing population of implants with longer follow-up. The reports are geographically dispersed, with no single account or surgeon responsible for a majority of the entries. Atlanta remains a higher-volume source of reports, but this is not materially different from its overall Apex utilization.

Lot review was completed for complaints where component lot information was available. The implicated cups, stems, and heads span multiple manufacturing periods and component lots. No individual cup lot, stem lot, or head lot represents a meaningful concentration of the metal-ion/ARMD-related complaints. In particular, there is no repeated lot pattern that would support a discrete manufacturing containment action at this time. The current distribution is more consistent with a wear-related or use-condition-related pattern than with a single manufacturing-related event. This conclusion should remain provisional pending receipt of additional implant and surgical-positioning information.

Nine events in the H1 population involve confirmed revision surgery. Explant analysis has been completed or preliminarily reviewed for seven of those cases; the remaining two explants are either with the hospital pathology department or pending return to Veridian. The available analyses describe polished wear areas, linear or arcuate surface scars, and in several cases damage patterns at the cup rim/head interface. Where operative records and radiographs were provided, the cases generally involved higher reported cup inclination angles.

These observations are consistent with the elevated-angle wear concern previously identified in the 2019 engineering re-analysis. As discussed at the time, the standard test configuration did not evaluate all surgical orientations observed in clinical practice. Quality is not making a causal determination based on complaint data alone; however, the alignment between the explant observations and the prior wear-test findings warrants continued close monitoring.

MDR assessments have been completed for all reportable events received through the reporting cutoff. Required submissions have been made within the applicable timelines, and the MDR log is current as of June 30. A small number of files remain open for follow-up medical records and device-return information, but no reportable event is presently overdue for evaluation or filing.

Recommended actions are as follows:

1. Continue monthly ApexHip complaint trending, with a separate review of metal-ion, ARMD, and revision events.
2. Maintain enhanced follow-up requests for radiographs, cup inclination information, metal-ion laboratory values, and explant returns.
3. Provide the updated trend data to Post-Market Surveillance for comparison against available registry data.
4. Reassess whether escalation to a formal cross-functional signal review is appropriate if the current reporting rate continues through Q3.

Legal has been informally briefed regarding the volume increase and the nature of the allegations. No change to the current complaint-handling procedure is proposed at this time.

Priya

Date: April 1, 2022

Product: ApexHip Metal-on-Metal Total Hip System
Reporting Period: January 1–March 31, 2022
Subject: Q1 2022 metal-ion complaint trending summary

Per the complaint-trending procedure, Quality reviewed all ApexHip complaints closed or opened during Q1 2022 with reported elevated cobalt and/or chromium values, suspected ARMD, tissue reaction, or revision associated with metal debris. Duplicate reports concerning the same patient event were consolidated where identifiable.

A total of 19 metal-ion-related ApexHip complaints were recorded during Q1 2022, compared with 12 during Q1 2021. The increase is concentrated in territories where the product has historically had greater utilization and where follow-up laboratory values are being obtained more consistently.

| Region | Q1 2022 Complaints | Revision Outcome Reported |
|---|---:|---:|
| Southeast | 7 | 5 |
| Nashville | 4 | 3 |
| Denver | 3 | 2 |
| Other | 5 | 4 |
| Total | 19 | 14 |

Of the 19 complaints, 14 include confirmation that revision surgery occurred or had been scheduled based on the latest information provided by the treating facility or surgeon. The remaining five reports involve ongoing surveillance, imaging, repeat laboratory testing, or a recommendation for clinical follow-up. Complaint files remain subject to update as additional operative and explant information is received.

Serum cobalt values were available in 16 of the 19 complaint records. The average reported serum cobalt level among those complainants was 41 ppb. This is materially above the generally cited normal range of less than 1 ppb in individuals without a cobalt-containing implant. Chromium values were also elevated in a majority of records, although reporting units and collection timing were not uniform enough to calculate a comparable aggregate without further normalization.

The observed trend continues to track with the pattern Halvorsen’s engineering team identified in prior wear testing, including increased wear under non-standard cup positioning conditions. Quality is continuing to process each event per procedure, including MDR assessment where applicable, and will provide the underlying TrackWise extract to Regulatory and PMS for their respective review.

TO: Rob Castellano, Chief Executive Officer; Rachel Steinberg, General Counsel
FROM: Owen Park, Chief Financial Officer
DATE: October 26, 2021
SUBJECT: Preliminary Financial Exposure Note – Registry Signal Decision
CONFIDENTIAL / PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL WORK PRODUCT

Following our discussion last week regarding the September 14 Registry Signal Review meeting, I asked Hannah Berg to help model out our potential downstream exposure. As we finalized the path to maintain ApexHip commercial distribution supported by a labeling update and the upcoming Dear Doctor advisory, we need to understand the financial parameters should the registry trends in the UK (NJR) and domestic tracking (AJRR) fail to stabilize over the next 12 to 24 months.

Please note that this analysis is strictly exploratory and does not reflect a formal accounting position or GAAP accrual.

Scenario Modeling (FY 2022–2024 Outlook)

Our projections hinge on two primary variables: continued commercial volume and actual cumulative revision divergence against historical class baselines. At our current run-rate (~14,000 systems annually at ~$9,800 ASP), a continued divergence toward the 7.1% 5-year revision rate flagged by the NJR introduces predictable indemnity and defense tailwinds.

| Scenario | Modeled Revision Uplift | Est. System Volume (3-Yr) | Potential Claims Exposure / Reserve Range |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Low Case | +1.5% to 2.0% over class average | 32,000 units (assumes tapering) | $8.0M – $11.5M |
| Mid Case | +3.0% to 3.5% over class average | 38,000 units (steady adoption) | $14.0M – $18.5M |
| High Case | +4.0%+ over class average | 42,000 units (aggressive growth) | $20.0M – $25.0M |

*Low Case* assumes our surgical technique labeling updates take hold, mitigating edge-loading outliers, with claims limited primarily to concentrated revisions and modest legal defense. *High Case* contemplates persistent ARMD and ion-related complications driving formal litigation across multiple territories, forcing substantial per-case settlements.

Recommendations

At present, ASC 450 (Contingencies) criteria for an accrual are not met; loss is neither probable nor reasonably estimable given the lack of active filed litigation and the uncertain causal link to technique versus manufacturing.

1. Maintain Current Stance: Do not book a formal balance sheet reserve for Q3 or FY21 year-end.
2. Quarterly Registry Monitoring: Finance should receive direct quarterly syntheses from Greg Novak's team to track NJR and AJRR curve inflections against these sensitivity bands.

Subject: ISO 14242 Wear Test Report – ApexHip Supplemental Inclination Study

Dear Mr. Halvorsen:

At Veridian Orthopedics’ request, Meridian Testing Labs conducted a supplemental simulator wear study of the ApexHip metal-on-metal total hip bearing under elevated acetabular cup inclination. This work was requested as an extension of the previously completed ISO 14242 protocol testing conducted at the standard 45-degree cup orientation.

Study Objective
The objective was to compare volumetric wear, visual bearing surface condition, and cobalt/chromium release rates for ApexHip constructs tested at 55 degrees inclination against the established 45-degree control configuration.

Test Articles
Six ApexHip bearing constructs were evaluated. Test articles consisted of Co/Cr acetabular cups from the V-2100 series and matching Co/Cr femoral heads from the H-3050 series. The cup lots included V-2108, V-2113, and V-2121; head lots included H-3052, H-3057, and H-3061. Components were supplied by Veridian and inspected upon receipt for packaging integrity and visible defects. No pre-test anomalies were observed.

Methodology
Testing was performed using six-station hip joint simulators in accordance with ISO 14242 loading and motion profiles, except for the specified acetabular orientation. Three stations were configured at 45 degrees inclination and served as controls. Three stations were configured at 55 degrees inclination. All stations were operated for 5 million cycles at 1 Hz under bovine serum lubricant diluted to 25 g/L total protein concentration. Lubricant was changed at 0.5 million-cycle intervals.

Gravimetric measurements were taken at each lubricant interval after cleaning and drying pursuant to laboratory procedure MTL-WEAR-014. Lubricant samples were retained at each interval and analyzed by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry for cobalt and chromium content. Bearing surfaces were examined by optical microscopy at completion.

Results
The 45-degree control group demonstrated cumulative volumetric wear consistent with prior ApexHip simulator work. The 55-degree group showed a material increase beginning between 1.0 and 1.5 million cycles, with the differential increasing through the end of the study.

| Configuration | Mean Cumulative Wear at 5M Cycles | Mean Co/Cr Release Rate |
|---|---:|---:|
| 45-degree inclination | 14.2 mm³ | 0.18 mg/million cycles |
| 55-degree inclination | 71.6 mm³ | 0.94 mg/million cycles |

The elevated-inclination group therefore exhibited approximately five times the volumetric wear and metal ion release rate observed in the 45-degree control group. Two of three 55-degree stations also demonstrated localized polishing and stripe wear near the superior rim of the cup, consistent with edge-loading contact. These features were not observed to the same extent in the control group.

Conclusion
Under the conditions tested, elevated cup inclination materially increased wear of the ApexHip metal-on-metal bearing. Clinical cup positioning above approximately 50 degrees inclination presents an elevated risk of edge loading, increased wear volume, and increased cobalt/chromium release relative to the standard 45-degree orientation.

This report is provided to Mr. Halvorsen for internal distribution to the Veridian design team. It should be considered together with the applicable design inputs, risk analysis, and clinical evaluation materials.

Sincerely,

Meridian Testing Labs

Elaine Porter, Ph.D.
Director, Biomechanical Evaluation Services
